earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog: 'no data for Nde-Gbite was ever recorded' (retired languoid; Blench 1999 got only secondhand info)

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2020. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages (4th ed., ms., Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation).
sources.note: No entry for Nde-Gbite at all; 'Antere' appears only under Yamba (483). The 'Nde' entries are the Bakor-cluster Nde of Cross River State (Nde-Nsele-Nta), a different language.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2012. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages, 3rd edition (ms.).
sources.note: No entry for Nde-Gbite; no mention of Gbite/Antere.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 1999. Field trip to record the status of some little-known Nigerian languages. Ogmios (Newsletter of the Foundation for Endangered Languages) 11: 11-14.
sources.note: Nothing. p.13: Blench could not reach Antere; Antere people met in Yerimaru listed the groups/languages of Antere, including a people 'speaking (?) Ndəgbite'. No data of any kind was recorded for it (only a Viti wordlist was taken).

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page ndeg1238 Nde-Gbite (Hammarström et al.), Bookkeeping comment.
sources.note: Nothing; states 'no data for Nde-Gbite was ever recorded and no specific village location.. is given. Since the language is unattested and not specifically located, it cannot be asserted to be different from all other languages.'

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority, code page 'ned' Nde-Gbite (SIL).
sources.note: Nothing; code still Active, individual living language.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Viti language' (Nde-Gbite language redirects here; infobox lists ned/ndeg1238 as a second code of Viti [vit], viti1241).
Eberhard, David M., Gary F. Simons & Charles D. Fennig (eds.). 2025. Ethnologue: Languages of the World, 28th ed. Dallas: SIL International. Entry: Nde-Gbite [ned].
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Only to confirm what Ethnologue's entry rests on (expected: Blench 1999 second-hand report, no data); will not contain a stress statement.

sources.citation: Any future field documentation of the languages of Antere village (Taraba State, Sardauna LGA, on the Cameroon border) — e.g. a survey by Blench/Connell or SIL Nigeria covering Viti (Vɨtɨ) [vit] and the reported 'Ndəgbite'.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Only new fieldwork could establish whether Nde-Gbite exists as a distinct variety and what its prosody is; Blench 1999 guessed the Antere lects are Grassfields Bantu (which would typically be tonal).

sources.citation: Eberhard, Simons & Fennig (eds.), Ethnologue: Languages of the World, entry Nde-Gbite [ned].
sources.note: not reachable by automated download; Ethnologue entries of this kind carry no phonology anyway, and Glottolog reports the entry derives solely from Blench 1999's second-hand report.
